Sell Feet Pics in Australia

The slow start and the buyer who wants to pay off the app are the two problems that catch new Australian sellers. Tax is the third, and it does not wait for a big year.

Dark-Ero editorialUpdated 2026-11-1018+

At a glance

FeetFinder, Fun With Feet, OnlyFans and Fansly are among the shops that can pay an Australian seller.

Content income is generally assessable, and the resident tax-free threshold is not a feet-pic exemption.

Payouts are often in US dollars, then converted by a bank or a wallet.

Key takeaways

  • You have to be 18 or older, and each shop checks identity before a cash-out.
  • FeetFinder sellers keep 85 or 90 percent and can request a payout from a US$30 balance.
  • Fun With Feet charges a listing fee and advertises no commission on the sale.
  • OnlyFans and Fansly keep 20 percent, so you keep 80 percent.
  • This is general information, not advice from a registered tax agent.

Adults in Australia can sell feet pics on sites that accept Australian sellers, and they can keep a face out of every file. The ATO generally treats money from creating content as assessable income, whether you call it a business or a side hustle.

The long comparison of eight shops is sell feet pics in Australia. Some currencies still have to be confirmed inside the account before you pay a plan.

Whether you need an ABN or GST registration depends on the activity and the ATO's own tests. This page is general information, not a ruling.

Disclosure: Dark-Ero is independent, with no affiliate link on this page. Adults 18+ only.

Shops that pay Australia

A dedicated feet marketplace is the simplest first shelf if you have no audience, which is why our FeetFinder review leads with published fees. You keep 85 percent on Basic or 90 percent on Premium, and you can request a payout once the available balance reaches US$30.

Basic is US$4.99 a month, US$14.99 a year or US$40 lifetime, and Premium is US$14.99 a month, US$49.99 a year or US$80 lifetime. Buyers pay inside the shop, and the seller agreement bars taking content payments through PayPal, Paxum or another outside service.

On yearly billing, Premium costs more up front and keeps an extra five points, so it pulls ahead only after sales are large enough to cover that gap. On monthly billing the gap is US$10, which is why a quiet account should stay on the cheaper plan.

Fun With Feet charges a listing fee instead of a cut of each sale. The seller help lists $9.99 for one month or $14.99 for three months, and our Fun With Feet review is the place to read the catch.

The ranking site's pass on that shop is the Fun With Feet review. The plan page does not always name the currency, and withdrawals are described from a $50 balance, so confirm both in an Australian account before you pay.

OnlyFans takes 20 percent of each fan payment, so you keep 80 percent, and there is no seller plan. Discovery is the catch, because a profile with no audience of its own can sit unseen.

Fansly also keeps 20 percent of subscriptions, media, messages and tips. The hold and the minimums are in our Fansly review, including a published US$20 Paxum floor and a higher one for an international bank transfer.

Check which payout methods an Australian Fansly account actually shows, because the menu can differ from the help page. A method you cannot withdraw to is not a method.

How the money comes home

Sellers outside the US are commonly paid through Paxum, or through Masspay where the shop offers it. You then send the money to an Australian bank, and the wallet or the bank may charge to turn US dollars into Australian dollars.

A mid-October 2026 Reserve Bank rate used in the source check put US$30 near A$43. Your provider can use a different rate, so budget the conversion instead of spending the US dollar figure as if it were already Australian.

PayID is handy between Australian banks, and it shows the payer the name linked to it. Do not give a buyer your PayID, your bank details, or a personal payment app when the shop's terms require its own checkout.

Keep the selling money in a separate account so tax time is a ledger rather than a guess. That separation does not hide your identity from someone who is allowed to pay you.

What the ATO is likely to see

The ATO's content-creator guidance treats this money as income you may have to report. Residents who can claim the full tax-free threshold pay no income tax on the first A$18,200 of taxable income, and that line covers the job plus the side income together.

A student example in the source material earned A$9,000 from casual work and A$3,000 profit from feet pics, which is A$12,000 and under the threshold, so no income tax was due in that sketch. They might still need to lodge a return, and the Medicare levy is a separate question.

Since 1 July 2024 the Sharing Economy Reporting Regime can require platforms to report seller and transaction details to the ATO. A report is not itself a tax bill, and it is a reason to keep your own records.

The UK allowance is a different number, explained in how to sell feet pics in the UK. Do not import a British £1,000 rule into an Australian return.

US self-employment tax is likewise the wrong form, which our FeetFinder taxes page is frank about. FeetFinder still asks non-US sellers for a W-8BEN, and that form does not replace the Australian return.

The ranking site's US tax note is FeetFinder taxes. Use it only to see what the shop asks Americans to file.

Fee shopping across the category starts at feet marketplaces. Compare the plan you would actually pay, not the headline share.

The FeetFinder review is the outside fee check if you want a second read before you subscribe. Confirm the currency on the button you are about to press.

Verdict

Pick a shop that will actually pay an Australian account, keep the chat on that shop, and treat the income as taxable from the first dollar you might have to report. US dollar payouts are not Australian dollars until a bank says they are.

Ask a registered tax agent if the ABN or GST question is live for you. Adults only, and this page is not that advice.

FAQ

Can I sell feet pics from Australia?

Yes, if you are 18 or older and the shop accepts Australian sellers and pays out to a method you can use. FeetFinder, Fun With Feet, OnlyFans and Fansly are the usual names to compare.

Do I pay Australian tax on feet pics?

The ATO generally treats content income as assessable. The resident tax-free threshold of A$18,200 covers all of your taxable income together, not this work on its own.

Do I need an ABN?

Not every seller does, and you need one before you can register for GST. Whether you are in business is an ATO question, so ask a registered tax agent if you are unsure.

How do Australian sellers get paid on FeetFinder?

You request a payout from a US$30 available balance, commonly through Paxum or Masspay. The shop pays in US dollars, and your bank or wallet may charge to convert them.

Does Fansly keep the same share as OnlyFans?

Both keep 20 percent of the fan payments those terms describe, so you keep 80 percent. Fansly's published minimums differ by payout method.

Should I give a buyer my PayID?

No, PayID shows the name linked to it, and several shops ban off-platform payments entirely. Take the sale through the shop's checkout.
